title: Pain under the foot (plantar fasciitis)
intro: Plantar fasciitis is one of the most common causes of heel pain. It affects the thick band of tissue running under the foot from the heel to the toes. The pain is typically worst with the first steps in the morning. Most people recover within months with stretching, suitable footwear and activity changes.

sections.heading: Causes and risk factors
paragraphs: The plantar fascia supports the arch of the foot and absorbs stress. Repeated strain can cause small tears and irritation. Risk factors include overweight, long periods standing or walking, a sudden increase in running, tight calf muscles, high or flat arches and unsupportive or worn shoes.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: The typical pain is a stabbing or aching feeling under the heel, worst after rest, such as the first steps after getting up, and may ease after a few minutes of walking, only to return after long standing. Swelling and redness are unusual and suggest other causes.

sections.heading: What helps
paragraphs: Reduce activities that provoke pain, such as running or prolonged standing, and replace them with low-impact exercise such as cycling or swimming. Stretching the calf and the sole of the foot several times daily is helpful, including stretching before getting out of bed. Wear supportive shoes with cushioning, avoid walking barefoot on hard floors and consider cushioned heel pads or arch supports. Losing weight eases the load.

sections.heading: Further treatment
paragraphs: Painkillers or anti-inflammatory gels may ease pain. A physiotherapist can add strengthening exercises and taping. Corticosteroid injections can give short-term relief but may weaken the tissue and are used sparingly. Shock-wave therapy is sometimes used for stubborn cases, with mixed evidence. Surgery is rarely needed.
Seek advice if pain follows an injury, if there is numbness, a swollen or hot heel, or if pain persists beyond several weeks of self-care.

sections.heading: Prevention
paragraphs: Wear supportive shoes, replace worn running shoes, build up exercise gradually, keep calf muscles flexible and maintain a healthy weight. Avoid long periods on hard floors without cushioning.

examples.title: Morning routine
examples.text: Imagine your first steps each morning are painful. You could stretch your calves and foot arch gently before standing, wear supportive slippers and avoid barefoot walking on hard floors.

examples.title: Adjusting activity
examples.text: Suppose you are a runner with heel pain. You might switch to cycling or swimming for a few weeks, check your shoes and return to running gradually.
